facts.text: The community's name originates from the Rawls family and the natural mineral springs discovered in the vicinity, which were initially called Heckla by Choctaw people before being renamed.
Originally called Heckla by Choctaw settlers who found the springs while foraging for cane, a post office opened in 1895, changing to Rawls Springs in 1905.
Historically known for its mineral springs with reputed healing properties, the area developed as a health resort in the early 20th century, attracting visitors until operations ceased by 1936.
Rawls Springs is located on the former Illinois Central Gulf Railroad.
Benjamin Rawles (also spelled Rawls) settled the area in 1833, establishing one of the first homesteads near the Bouie River amid dense pine forests rich in wildlife.
The community continues to honor its heritage through local landmarks like the former Rawls Springs Hotel site and ongoing genealogical interest in early settlers.
